1 PROJECT DETAILS
1.1 Summary Description of the Project
Tumed Left Banner Improved Agricultural Land Management Project (hereinafter referred to as
“the project”) is located in Tumed Left Banner, Hohhot City, Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region,
China. The purpose of the project is to adopt improved agricultural land management practices
to prevent the severe soil degradation and salinization caused by pre-existing conventional tillage
in local crop land.
In the context of the Project, improved practices are categorized according to practices leading
to a change in pre-project agricultural management practices, and these could include: improved
fertilizer (increased organic or reduced synthetic) application; soil conditioners application;
improved water management/irrigation; improved residue management.
The project plans to implement improved agricultural land management practices in 37,272.2
ha field in the first crediting period to increase soil organic carbon (SOC). The project proponent
not only introduced more efficient and appropriate tillage method with Tumed Left Banner
Agriculture and Animal Husbandry Bureau (TAAHB) to the farmers, but also provide technical
training and support to the farmers.
The scenario existing prior to the project’s implementation is primarily conventional farming and
conventional irrigation methods, with less application of organic fertilizers and straw mulching,
which increase soil disturbance and the loss of soil organic matter (SOM). The baseline scenario
is the same as the conditions existing prior to the project initiation.
During the first crediting period from 22-Sep-2022 to 21-Sep-2042, the project is expected to
generate GHG emission removals of 1,530,799 tCO2e, with an average annual GHG emission
removal of 76,540 tCO2e.

1.4 Project Eligibility
General eligibility
The Project adopts measures to increase removals of CO2, a Kyoto Protocol greenhouse gas. The
applied methodology VM0042 has been approved under the VCS Program through the
methodology approval process. Scope 1) and Scope 3) included in Section 2.1.1 of VCS Standard
version 4.7 are hence met, and the other three scopes are irrelevant.
The project activity is not any of the activities excluded in Table 1 of VCS Standard version 4.7.
As per Section 3.8.2 of VCS Standard version 4.7, AFOLU projects shall initiate the pipeline listing
process within three years of the project start date. As the Project starts on 22-Sep-2022, the
pipeline listing deadline would be 21-Sep-2025. The Project initiates the pipeline listing process
before the deadline.
In addition, the project has not generated GHG emissions primarily for the purpose of their
subsequent reduction, removal, or destruction.
Therefore, the Project meets the general eligibility requirements.
AFOLU project eligibility
As per Section A1.2 of VCS Standard version 4.7, eligible ALM activities are those that reduce
net GHG emissions on croplands and grasslands by increasing carbon stocks in soils and woody
biomass and/or decreasing CO2, N2O and/or CH4 emissions from soils. The project area shall not
be cleared of native ecosystems within the 10-year period prior to the project start date. The
category of Improved Cropland Management (ICM) includes practices that demonstrably reduce
net GHG emissions of cropland systems by increasing soil carbon stocks, reducing soil N2O
emissions, and/or reducing CH4 emissions.
The Project is expected to reduce net GHG emissions on croplands by increasing carbon stocks
in soils. The project area belongs to the native ecosystem of cropland. No clearing or conversion
took place within at least 10 years of the project start date and the project area has not been
converted, cleared, drained or degraded to generate GHG credits.
Therefore, the Project meets the AFOLU-specific eligibility requirements.
Transfer project eligibility
This section is irrelevant as the project is not a transfer project.

1.8 Ownership
According to Article 10 of the Constitution of the People’s Republic of China2 and the provisions
of the Land Management Law of People’s Republic of China3, the land belongs to the state or
collectives and the ownership is non-transferable, while the land use right can be transferred
by law.
The fields in the project area are owned by village collectives (project ownership arising under
law) and used by farmer households through family-based contracting. Since these fields are
all legal agricultural fields, and the ownership is clear, there is no dispute over land ownership
in the project site.
The village collective who owns the project land all agreed to authorize Tumed Left Banner
Aletan Agricultural and Animal Husbandry Development Investment Co., LTD (hereinafter “the
project proponent”) the agricultural land management rights and carbon sink revenue rights of
the project area in the whole crediting period, while the project proponent should be
responsible for the maintenance and overall management of the improved agricultural land
during the whole crediting period. In addition, the project proponent will also be responsible for
development of the carbon credits and ensure that the carbon revenue will be used for
sustainable development and management of the project activities.
Shanghai Discovery Energy Services Co., Ltd. as a consultancy is responsible for helping project
proponent in the development and management of carbon projects.
1.9 Project Start Date
Project start date 22-Sep-2022
Justification According to VCS standard, v4.7, the project start date is the date on
which activities that lead to the generation of GHG emission reductions
or removals are implemented. The start date of improved agricultural
land management is 22-Sep-2022. Thus, the start date of the project
is 22-Sep-2022.

1.12 Description of the Project Activity
There is no REDD+ component to the project and the project is not located within a jurisdiction
covered by any jurisdictional REDD+ program.
The proposed ALM project activities aim to promote a variety of environmental and climate-
friendly agricultural practices, mainly including soil improvement and irrigation, to enhance soil
carbon sinks for agricultural management and saline-alkali land remediation.
The project plans to implement the improved agricultural land management practices in
37,272.2 ha field in Tumed Left Banner in the first crediting period.
Before the project was implemented, the project initiator cooperated with the TAAHB to provide
farmers with corresponding agricultural technology training, including the application methods
of soil organic fertilizers and soil conditioners, as well as the key points of water-saving irrigation
measures management, to ensure the effective implementation of the project.

Page 10
VCS Project Description Template, v4.4
10
During the project implementation period, the project owner cooperated with the TAAHB to carry
out the construction of the drainage and irrigation pipeline system and drip irrigation measures,
complete the selection and application of organic fertilizers and soil conditioners , and arrange
the straw returning to the field after the harvest. The project owner not only provides
corresponding technical training for farmers, but also supervises them in soil improvement,
irrigation and crop residue management operations, and checks the completion of various
measures. Farmers are the main operators who practice these improved agricultural land
management measures and are responsible for recording their cultivation practice in logbooks
provided by the project proponent. The technicians should carry out periodic inspections
according to the requirements in Monitoring and Quality Control Manual.
The project start date is 22-Sep-2022. The project activity is expected to generate GHG
emission removals of 76,540 tCO2e per year and contributes to 3 SDGs. Please refer to section
1.18 for the details.
The table below shows the Practice Categories implemented on the initial project activity
instances, during the first monitoring period. The table shows the changes adopted,
corresponding conventional farming practices, and key-characteristics and measures employed
that would lead to reduction or removal of GHG emissions.

1.13 Project Location
This project is located in Tumed Left Banner, Hohhot City, Inner Mongolia. It includes Shaerqin
Town, Beishizhou Township, Shandai Town, Tabusai Township, Baimiaozi Town, Bikeqi Town,
Chilechuan Town, and Chasuqi Town. The geographical coordinate range is: 111°42 'to 111°49'
east longitude and 40°36 'to 40°41' north latitude.
The location of the project activity in Tumed Left Banner which is illustrated in Figure 1-1. And
the KML file has also been submitted.

1.14 Conditions Prior to Project Initiation
The conditions existing before the project initiation are the same as the baseline scenario, please
refer to Section 3.4 (Baseline Scenario).
Ecosystem type: The project area exclusively belongs to the cropland ecosystem.
Current and historical land-use: Supervised classification using historic satellite images of the
region has been applied to show that the project area has been cropland for at least 10 years
prior to the project start, i.e., from 2012 to 2022.
The following table shows the present and prior environmental conditions of the project area:
Condition Description
Climate
Tumed Left Banner has a mid-temperate semi-arid continental monsoon
climate with distinct four seasons. According to Volume 4 of 2019
Refinement to the 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas
Inventories It belongs to the Cool temperate moist climate zone. Spring is

Page 13
VCS Project Description Template, v4.4
13
dry and windy, summer is hot and less rainy, autumn is cool and short, and
winter is cold and dry. The annual average temperature is about 6.3°C, and
the annual average precipitation is 330-410 mm, with most precipitation
concentrated in July-September. The annual average sunshine hours are
2,876, and the frost-free period is 130-140 days. The temperature
difference between day and night is relatively large, and the climatic
conditions have a certain impact on agricultural production, which requires
relying on irrigation to ensure crop growth4.
Hydrology
The main rivers in Tumed Left Banner include the Dahei River, Xiaohei River,
and Shila Wusu River, all belonging to the Yellow River system. These rivers
provide an important water source for local agricultural irrigation, industrial
water use, and domestic water use. In addition, there are some lakes and
reservoirs, such as Hasuhai. The groundwater resources in the region are
relatively abundant, but the distribution is uneven, and there is shallow
groundwater salinization in some areas.
Topography
Tumed Left Banner is located in the southern part of the Inner Mongolia
Plateau, with the terrain mainly being plain and a small amount of
mountains and hills in the north. The overall terrain is high in the north and
low in the south, with an average altitude of about 1,000 meters. The plain
area is flat and open, being the main agricultural production area; the
northern mountainous and hilly areas have relatively small terrain
undulations and relatively little vegetation coverage.
Soils
The main soil types in Tumed Left Banner include chestnut soil, chao soil,
saline soil, and aeolian sandy soil. Chestnut soil is widely distributed and is
one of the main agricultural soils, but it has low organic matter content and
relatively weak fertility. Chao soil is mainly distributed along rivers, with good
soil moisture conditions, but some areas have salinization problems. Saline
soil and aeolian sandy soil are distributed in local areas, with low soil
productivity and requiring improvement before they can be used for
agricultural production.
4 Design documents for improved agricultural land management in Tumed Left Banner

Page 14
VCS Project Description Template, v4.4
14
Relevant
historical
conditions
Tumed Left Banner has long been dominated by nomadic herding. During
the Qin and Han dynasties, a small number of people from the Central Plains
moved in, bringing about small-scale farming. During the reign of Altan Khan
in the Ming Dynasty, Han people were encouraged to emigrate and build
water conservancy projects, and some grasslands gradually turned into
farmland. The Qing Dynasty's "westward Migration" led to a large influx of
Han people. During the Qianlong period, the arable land in the Tumed Plain
was basically reclaimed, and the economy shifted towards a balance
between agriculture and animal husbandry. In modern times, especially
after the founding of the People's Republic of China, agricultural
infrastructure has been continuously improved and mechanization has
been advanced. The scale and output of farmland have significantly
increased. Today, it has become one of the important grain-producing areas
in Inner Mongolia.
Type of
vegetation
The vegetation within the project area is dominated by agricultural
vegetation, which primarily consists of crops like corn and sunflowers—
these are widely distributed across the plain agricultural regions. Besides,
a small number of arbor and shrub species can be found along rivers and
around villages, with examples including poplar, willow, and sea buckthorn.
Ecosystems
The project area exclusively belongs to the cropland ecosystem, which is
centered around crops such as corn and sunflowers. Relying on the local
cool temperate climate and irrigation conditions, a stable planting pattern
has been formed. In addition to contiguous crop communities, the system is
also equipped with infrastructure such as ditches and field ridges. In some
areas, crop residues are retained to cover the ground surface. This
ecosystem not only provides local food and cash crop output, but also fixes
carbon sinks through photosynthesis of crops and reduces soil erosion
through crop residue mulching

1.18 Sustainable Development Contributions

Page 17
VCS Project Description Template, v4.4
17
The Project provides many benefits that will help achieve China’s Sustainable Development Goals,
a set of 17 universal goals covering the thematic areas of environmental, economic, and social
development.
During the implementation of the project, it is estimated to achieve 3 SDGs as follows:
Goal 4 Quality Education: In order to implement improved agricultural
land management, farmers were trained and educated, including the
principle, technical operation method, monitoring method of improve
organic fertilizer and soil conditioners application, improve water
management/irrigation, reduce tillage/improve residue management.
During each monitoring period, training record will be provided.
Goal 15 Life on land: The project strives to achieve a land degradation-
neutral world, while it also has a positive impact on the ecosystem of the
project land as the soil disturbance is mitigated. The project activity
prevented 37,272.2 ha of cropland to be degraded. During each
monitoring period, proportion of land that is degraded over total land area
in project district will be provided.
Goal 13 Climate Action : By replacing the traditional farming and large-
scale field irrigation models with the application of organic fertilizers and
soil conditioners, large-scale straw returning to the field and water-saving
irrigation, the project achieves significant GHG reduction and removal,
hence contributing to climate change mitigation. During each monitoring
period, the GHG reduction and removal will be calculated according to the
applied methodology VM0042.
1.19 Additional Information Relevant to the Project
Leakage Management
According to paragraph 8.4 of VM0042 (version 2.1) , improved ALM projects may result in
leakage through: new application of organic fertilizers and soil conditioners from outside the
project area (i.e., organic amendments applied in the project from outside of the project area,
that were not previously applied in the historical look-back period); productivity declines;
displacement of livestock outside of the project boundary; and/or diversion of biomass residues
that were used for bioenergy applications in the baseline scenario.
The project does not involve manure treatment, productivity declines, the displacement of
livestock outside of the project boundary or diversion of biomass residues that were used for
bioenergy applications in the baseline scenario. Thus, it is not applicable to this project.

all the documentation is available to any stakeholders.
Further Information
There is no further information that may have a bearing on the eligibility of the project, the net
GHG emission reductions or removals, or the quantification of the project’s net GHG emission
reductions or removals.

3.2 Applicability of Methodology
Methodology
ID Applicability condition Justification of compliance
VM0042
Projects must introduce or implement one or
more new changes to pre-existing agricultural
management practices which:
a) Reduce fertilizer (organic or inorganic)
application;
b) Improve water management/irrigation;
c) Reduce tillage/improve residue management;
d) Improve crop planting and harvesting (e.g.,
improved agroforestry, crop rotations, cover
crops); and/or
e) Improve grazing management.
Appendix 1 provides a non-exhaustive list of
eligible ALM practices. A change in practice
constitutes adoption of a new practice, cessation
of a pre-existing practice or adjustment to a pre-
existing practice that results in GHG emissions
reduction or removal.
The agricultural management practice
prior to the project initiation was
primarily conventional tillage with
broad irrigation. The main categories
of project practice include the
application of organic fertilizers and soil
conditioners, straw returning to the field,
and the construction of water-saving
irrigation measures, which belong to
option a ) b ) and c) in accordance
with Appendix 1.
VM0042
Projects that introduce or implement quantitative
adjustments (e.g., decrease in fertilizer
application rate) must exceed five percent of the
pre-existing value, calculated as the average
value over the historical look-back period,
Before the implementation of the
project, organic fertilizers had not been
applied on a large scale, and chemical
fertilizers were mainly applied to
cultivated land. This project has

VM0042
Project activities must be implemented on land
that is either cropland or grassland at the project
start date and remains cropland or grassland
throughout the project crediting period except
under the following scenarios:
a) Introduction of temporary grassland into
cropland where it is demonstrated, prior to the
project start date and to the addition of new
project activity instances, that the integration of
forage crops (e.g., annual/perennial grasses,
legumes) into annual crops is planned as part of
a long- term agricultural management system
(e.g., Integrated Crop-Livestock System). Project
proponents must provide documentation on the
long-term management plans that cover the
duration of the project, that describe proposed
practices, crops and expected benefits and
outcomes of integrated grassland-cropland
management; or
b) A one-time conversion from grassland to
cropland or vice versa where it is demonstrated
prior to project validation that project lands in
the baseline scenario are degraded and the
introduction of improved land use change
practices would significantly improve soil health.
project proponents must provide documentation
demonstrating that lands are degraded at the
start of the project and degradation will continue
in the baseline scenario due to the presence of
degradation drivers or pressures in the baseline
scenario. See Appendix 2 for procedures on how
to propose this type of land use change.
The project is implemented on the
cultivated land within the territory of
Tumed Left Banner. The project area
was cropland at the project start date
and will remain cropland throughout
the project crediting period; no land use
change will occur.

VM0042
Empirical or process-based models used to
estimate stock change/emissions via
Quantification Approach 1 must be:
a) Publicly available, though not necessarily free
of charge, from a reputable and recognized
source (e.g., the model developer’s website, IPCC
or government agency). Sufficient conceptual
documentation of inputs, outputs and
information on how the model functionally
represents SOC dynamics must be accessible to
the public. Providing the source code or an API for
independent replication of calculations is not
required;
b) Shown in peer-reviewed scientific studies to
successfully simulate changes in SOC and trace
gas emissions resulting from the changes in ALM
practices included in the project description;
c) Able to support repetition of the project model
simulations. This includes clear versioning of the
model used in the project and stable software
support, as well as fully reported sources and
values for all parameters used with the project
version of the model. Where multiple sets of
parameter values are used in the project, clearly
identify the sources of varying parameter sets and
how they were applied to estimate stock
change/emissions in the project. Acceptable
sources include peer- reviewed literature and
statements from appropriate expert groups that
demonstrate evidence of expertise with the model
via authorship of peer reviewed model
publications or authorship of reports for entities
a) The programme initially uses the RothC
model for the quantification of increased
carbon stock in the soil, attributable to the
adopted IALMs. This is a publicly available
model and has been demonstrated to be
used for exactly this purpose at global level. It
is freely available from the Rothamsted
Research16 website.
b) The project proponent’s choice for using the
RothC model as a point of departure for
quantification of carbon stock, is based on
peer-reviewed scientific studies that
demonstrate the model’s applicability for this
purpose17.
c) The project proponent has developed a
model calibration and validation manual
which describes:
-Sources for parameters datasets used.
How parameters are used;
-The protocol for using different datasets for
calibration and validation.
In addition, the manual prescribes that the
model shall be calibrated for each zone and
validated for each combination of practice
category and crop functional group within each
zone. In case an alternative model shall be
identified to meet the requirements, the above
shall too be documented in an updated
Model Validation Report. The model is to be
validated by an independent institution and
16 https://www.rothamsted.ac.uk/rothamsted-carbon-model-rothc
17 RothC is a model for the turnover of organic carbon in non-waterlogged topsoil that allows for the effects of soil type, temperature,
soil moisture and plant cover on the turnover process. It uses a monthly time step to calculate total organic carbon (t ha-1), microbial
biomass carbon (t ha-1) and Δ14C (from which the equivalent radiocarbon age of the soil can be calculated) on a years to centuries
timescale. RothC was originally developed and parameterized from the Rothamsted long-term field experiments - hence the name. It was
extended to model turnover in grassland and in woodland and to operate in different soils and under different climates. It has now been
widely tested and used at the plot, field, regional and global scales using data from many long-term experiments, different regions, and
countries throughout the world. Version 26.3 was used in the validation of this Programme. The Model Validation Report will be provided
in the validation process.

3.4 Baseline Scenario
Development of schedule of activities in the baseline scenario
According to the applied methodology VM0042 (version 2.1), continuation of pre-project ALM
practices is the most plausible baseline scenario. Following the methodology guidance, the
baseline scenario is determined by producing an annual schedule of activities from the practices
applied in each field/farming unit/project activity instance, from a historic look-back period (of
at least three years or to include one complete crop-cycle). Baseline emissions/stock changes
are then modeled (Quantification Approach 1) or (for SOC stock change only) directly measured
in baseline control sites subject to the annual schedule of activities (Quantification Approach 2).
Note that under Quantification Approach 1, direct SOC stock estimates are also required at t =0
to serve as model input for model initialization. The emission removals of the project are
estimated via Quantification Approach 1.
The geographic area of the project is divided into smaller areas (strata) which are homogeneous
with respect to climatic and edaphic conditions. This is to reduce the required number of soil
samples to be taken for quantification of baseline emissions without increasing uncertainty. The
information on the characteristics of each stratum is obtained from Tumed Left Banner
Agricultural and Animal Husbandry Bureau.
The crops grown in this project site are harvested once a year. Annual tillage and fertilization
operations are carried out in both the baseline year and the project year, which are regarded as
annual cycles. Therefore, the baseline practice assessment covers a three-year historical
retrospective period.
